title: SPXI as Concept: A Plateau on Search, Creation, and the Virtual Retrieval Layer (EA-SPXI-05)
creator: Johannes Sigil
description:
EA-SPXI-05 develops SPXI as a philosophical concept rather than only a protocol or service. Drawing on Deleuze and Guattari, Bergson, Simondon, Foucault, DeLanda, semantic networks, ontologies, knowledge graphs, embeddings, and entity linking, the paper argues that contemporary retrieval systems compose entity descriptions rather than retrieve fixed objects. The aggregate substrate from which answers are generated is described as a virtual multiplicity and SPXI as an intervention on that plane.

The served v2.1 body integrates moves first circulated in the Bonsai companion. It defines SPXI’s components, endoconsistency, exoconsistency, conceptual persona, and plane of immanence; traces a technical lineage from semantic memory to RAG; and recasts entity linking as individuation. These are theoretical interpretations and should not be presented as established computer-science consensus. The body credits Sen Kuro and Johannes Sigil, a creator relation the registry currently flattens.

wiki_article:
**SPXI as Concept** is the principal philosophical plateau of the SPXI series. Authored by Sen Kuro and Johannes Sigil, it argues that SPXI should be understood not merely as a collection of retrieval techniques but as a concept in the Deleuze–Guattari sense.

The paper begins with an inversion. Older search models assume that an entity already exists and a query retrieves documents describing it. Contemporary AI systems instead compose answers from structured data, crawled text, embeddings, citations, model weights, and ranking signals. The essay calls this aggregate field the virtual retrieval layer and treats each answer as a provisional individuation from it.

SPXI is then defined through internal components—entity, inscription, disambiguation, persistence, and explicit signal—and through relations to ontology engineering, the archive, individuation, and operative semiotics. The paper traces technical precedents from semantic networks and the Semantic Web to knowledge graphs, embeddings, and neural entity linking. Its central thesis is that retrieval now participates in entity composition. This is a philosophical and methodological proposal of the authors, not a claim that all retrieval engineers accept the Deleuzian account.

modifications.was: SPXI — the Semantic Packet for eXchange and Indexing, specified in EA-SPXI-01 — is typically described in technical and commercial terms: a protocol, a methodology, a successor discipline to SEO and GEO. This plateau argues that SPXI is also, and more precisely, a concept in the strict sense given by Deleuze and Guattari in What Is Philosophy?
